package_info.why_malicious: This report does not describe a specific malicious package or code. Instead, it discusses general software supply chain risks, dependency management challenges, and common attack vectors such as dependency confusion, typosquatting, and open source repository attacks. No concrete malicious package or code is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected or unauthorized dependency updates (dependency confusion)
Installation of packages with names similar to popular dependencies (typosquatting)
Unexpected code execution during build or install phases (build tool attacks)
Unusual or unauthorized changes to open source repositories (open source repo attack)
file_indicators: Presence of dependencies with suspicious or lookalike names in manifest files (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml)
Unexpected scripts or binaries in build tool directories
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound network connections during build or install processes
Connections to domains not associated with legitimate package registries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor dependency manifests for suspicious or lookalike package names, audit build and install scripts for unauthorized code execution, and track network activity during dependency installation for unexpected external communications. Employ automated tools to scan for known vulnerable or malicious packages and regularly update dependencies to patched versions.
